The overhaul is complete and pushed to GitHub (`jun-4-2026-workbook-grader`, commits `227d505` + `a62f714`). Both macOS and iOS builds finish with **zero errors and zero warnings** (down from ~15 warnings), and the app ships with bilingual READMEs.

**How it was done:** a 58-agent audit workflow read every file and produced 113 candidate findings; 45 were adversarially verified (18 confirmed, 27 refuted). After implementing, a second 27-agent review workflow re-checked the entire diff before commit and caught 4 more issues, which I fixed.

**Hidden bugs fixed** (the most consequential):
- **Workbook grading could silently report "0/0"** when the model couldn't read the pages — it now throws a clear, localized error with advice, and grading error messages are fully bilingual.
- **AI photo cleanup failed silently** — the photo tab now shows a warning banner when cleanup was skipped or failed, and a "AI cleaned" badge with a one-tap revert to the original OCR text.
- **The microphone kept recording after a speech-recognition failure** — teardown now runs on every error path, idempotently, without firing contradictory delegate callbacks.
- **Photo OCR ignored your explicit 中文/English scan choice** for ambiguous text; it now only auto-detects in Auto/Both modes. Rapid photo re-selection also no longer races stale results (tasks cancel cleanly).
- **Silent data loss risks closed**: all four UserDefaults stores now log decode failures and keep a last-known-good backup that auto-restores; activity date keys are pinned to a POSIX/Gregorian formatter (no more corruption on non-Gregorian locales); vocabulary dedup/removal normalizes invisible Unicode; English vocab no longer shows fake "pinyin".
- **A build-breaker you'd have hit in Xcode**: session logs had been committed inside `SwiftMandarin/`, and a second log folder collided in the resource-copy phase. I removed them, gitignored the path, and added a project exception so it can't recur.

**Integration & features added:** photo and live-speech translations now feed Translation History and the Stats heatmap/streaks (previously only typed translations counted); accepting a spoken translation fills in both sides; History gained a direction filter, a no-matches state, and a clear-all confirmation; AI Settings gained a per-provider **Test Connection** round-trip plus Vision/JSON capability badges; the previously dead **Pinyin Position** setting now works (above/below/inline) and was added to iOS Settings; accessibility labels and provider-accurate progress text round out the HIG polish.

**Project hygiene:** the pbxproj shed 149 duplicate source entries and 43 legacy references (67KB → 19KB), `handoff.md` no longer ships inside the app bundle, empty microphone/speech usage descriptions (a latent iOS crash) were filled in, and dead template code was deleted.

**Localization & docs:** 47 new catalog keys with reviewed Chinese translations (608 total — script-verified that no existing entries changed and all format placeholders are intact); grammar-point explanations and language names now follow the in-app language toggle. `README.md` was refreshed and a complete `README.zh-Hans.md` was added, cross-linked at the top of both.

One thing I couldn't do from the CLI: live GUI smoke tests (language toggle on the new strings, Test Connection with a real API key, the cleanup banner flow). Those are reasoned-and-compile-verified; worth a quick manual pass when you next run the app.

The app is now backward compatible with iOS 17, committed and pushed to GitHub (`82130c4`). Both platforms build with zero errors and zero warnings at the new targets (iOS 17.0; macOS/visionOS stay at 26.2).

**How the port works** — every modern API is availability-gated with a real fallback, so newer OSes keep the full experience:

| Capability | iOS 17 | iOS 18–25 | iOS 26+ |
|---|---|---|---|
| Translate / Photo / Live Speech translation | Your configured AI provider | Apple on-device translation | Apple on-device translation |
| Word-tap lookups, screenshot & Shortcuts translation | AI provider | AI provider | Apple on-device |
| Live speech transcription | `SFSpeechRecognizer` | `SFSpeechRecognizer` | `SpeechAnalyzer` (fully on-device) |
| Apple Intelligence | — | — | ✓ |
| Tab bar / design | Classic tab bar, material effects | Sidebar-adaptable / material | Sidebar-adaptable / Liquid Glass |

**The key engineering pieces:**
- **Translation**: The SwiftUI `.translationTask` API (iOS 18+) can't be stored in views deploying to 17, so a version-agnostic `TranslationConfigurationBox` + an 18-only `TranslationTaskHost` mounted in the background now drive it. A surprise the compiler caught: the standalone `TranslationSession(installedSource:target:)` initializer used for word lookups is actually **iOS 26+**, not 18 — those paths now fall back to your AI provider on anything older, with a clear localized "configure an AI provider in Settings → AI" error if none is set up.
- **Speech**: `SpeechRecognitionService` was rebuilt around an engine protocol — the existing SpeechAnalyzer pipeline on 26+, and a new legacy `SFSpeechRecognizer` engine for iOS 17 (continuous partial results, transcript finalized on stop, a final-result-beats-error rule). The public API is unchanged, so no view code had to care.
- **Apple Intelligence**: all `@Generable` models and `LanguageModelSession` calls are gated to iOS 26 with accurate unavailability messages.
- **UI**: glass effects fall back to material backgrounds via small compat modifiers; iOS 17 gets the classic tab bar (the 8 tabs overflow into the system "More" item on iPhone); an iOS 18-only SF Symbol that would have rendered blank was replaced.

**Verification**: compiler-driven (lowering the target surfaces every unavailable API as an error — all resolved), then a 30-agent adversarial review of the port diff, which caught and I fixed: the blank-icon SF Symbol, untracked fire-and-forget AI fallback tasks in all three translation views (now cancel-before-replace), partial-translation loss when one sentence fails in the photo fallback, the legacy engine's final-vs-error race, and stale "built for iOS 26" About text. Both READMEs (English and 中文) now show iOS 17+ requirements with the feature matrix above.

One caveat: only the iOS 26.3 simulator runtime is installed on this Mac, so the port is compile-verified at target 17 but hasn't been runtime-tested on an actual iOS 17 device or simulator — worth a smoke test (especially live speech and AI-fallback translation) if you have an iOS 17 device or can download an older simulator runtime in Xcode.

Done. Created the branch **`jun-12-2026-ios17-compat`** (following the repo's date-topic naming convention), committed the pending changes (`848c80b` — only session logs were uncommitted; all app work was already in), and pushed it to GitHub with upstream tracking set.

The branch carries the full history of both recent efforts — the ship-ready overhaul (`227d505`) and the iOS 17 backward-compatibility port (`82130c4`) — so it's ready to open as a PR against `main` whenever you want.
